requirements.text: The Libra Scheduler will manage sequential and embarrassingly parallel batch jobs to be run on a homogenous Linux cluster.
The scheduler will enforce resource allocations according to user-centric priorities.
The scheduler will be dynamic, allowing for the reallocation of resources for emergency jobs.
The scheduler will be scalable, ensuring performance does not degrade with the addition of nodes and jobs.
The scheduler will be configurable to allow for various scheduling policies that incorporate QoS parameters.
The scheduler will be separable from the cluster management system.
The scheduler will provide administrative security.
The scheduler will provide at least a basic level of job accounting.
The scheduler will use the proportional stride-scheduling algorithm to ensure resource allocation reflects job share.
The scheduler will not support job migration for the purpose of decreasing resource fragmentation.
The maximum response time for the submission of a job will be 1 minute.
The scheduler will ensure that all jobs are completed with a 10% error allowance.
The maximum cost payable as submitted by the user will be the maximum cost charged to the user.
The Libra scheduler will be a sub-component of SGE.
All coding will be done in standard C.

The scheduler must implement Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) to restrict administrative functions (e.g., job cancellation, policy modification) to authorized users, and all administrative actions must be logged with a timestamp and user identity.
All inter-component communication between the Libra scheduler, SGE master, and execution nodes must be encrypted using TLS/SSL to prevent eavesdropping and man-in-the-middle attacks.

The scheduler must perform strict input validation and sanitization on all user-provided job parameters (e.g., budget, deadline, executable path) to prevent command injection or path traversal attacks.
The scheduler shall maintain a response time of under 1 minute for job submission and scheduling decisions under a load of up to 1000 concurrent jobs and 100 cluster nodes.
The scheduler shall implement role-based access control (RBAC) to restrict administrative commands (e.g., altering cost structures, job suspension) to authenticated users with 'admin' privileges.
In the event of a scheduler process failure, the system shall implement a checkpointing mechanism to recover the state of the job queue and resume scheduling without manual intervention.
The system shall achieve a Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF) of at least 720 hours under normal operational load.
The scheduler shall maintain a job scheduling latency of less than 500ms for a cluster size of up to 100 nodes and a submission rate of 50 jobs per second.
The scheduler shall process job submissions within 1 second under a sustained load of 10 concurrent submissions per second.
The scheduler shall ensure that 95% of jobs complete within 110% of the user-specified deadline, assuming accurate job execution time estimates.
The scheduler's memory footprint shall not exceed 256MB and CPU utilization shall not exceed 5% of a single core when managing up to 1,000 concurrent jobs.
